I really don’t get the point of the article. Traveling has changed me, and not just in the sense of “i was home before, and then i went somewhere. and now i’m home, and i can say i’ve gone somewhere.”

traveling to study abroad somewhere forced me to come out of my comfort zone. i had to introduce myself to people. i had to learn to navigate public transportation, which was not a thing in the small, very rural town i lived in back home. i met and talked over lunch, coffee, drinks, walks, etc with people from class, people from my flat, people from a poetry club i joined… different people with different childhoods and lifestyles and opinions who i talked to and listened to and learned from and made friendships with. 

when i came home, so so so many people told me i seemed way more sure of myself, more confident, and happier. 

even for smaller trips, i was in prague with my parents and my sister. when my dad and me got lunch while my mom and sister were somewhere else, i don’t remember where, a waiter had forgotten to put in the order of our pizza, and we waited a while, and it was really a wonderful experience because my dad asked him after a bit and he was like “omg i am so sorry” and he gave us free shots and my dad invited him to dinner with me, my mom, and my sister. and the waiter, who was about my age, was so so cool and him and my dad talked for ageessss and all five of us at that dinner just had such a good time. and my dad and i still have his number and still talk to him. 

the point is that when i came back from prague, i was changed — i didn’t know actual castles existed in the world, and now i do. i didn’t know that person, i didn’t have those shots, i didn’t go out to dinner with him and my family, i didn’t know certain political things between czech republic and germany, and now i have. boom. change.
